# Executive Summary

Senior program executive at NASA Headquarters bridging federal science investments and on-the-ground natural resource management. Ph.D. in Natural Resource Sciences; B.S. and M.S. in Wildlife Ecology and Conservation. Oversees a multi-project portfolio producing global Earth observation data, run by contractor teams at four U.S. NASA centers, and has built binding partnerships with Department of the Interior bureaus, state fish and wildlife agencies, Tribal-serving organizations, and conservation NGOs. Recognized with a FY26 NASA Headquarters Honor Award for "Excellence in National Benefits."

# Professional Experience

**Program Executive, Earth Science Data Systems (ESDS)**, Earth Science Division, Science Mission Directorate\
National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Headquarters, Washington, DC\
Nov 2024 – Present \textbar{} GS-0801-15 \textbar{} 40 hrs/wk \textbar{} Supervisor: Kathleen Baynes, (240) 343-4922; may contact

Executive oversight of NASA's operational global Earth data production portfolio, including Foundational Data Products (FDP), the Fire Information for Resource Management System (FIRMS), the Land, Atmosphere Near-real-time Capability for Earth Observations (LANCE), Science Investigator-led Processing Systems (SIPS), and the Earth Science Information Partners (ESIP) cooperative agreement. Portfolio of approximately \$40M per year, executed by contractor teams and project offices across four NASA centers.

- **ECQ 1 – Commitment to the Rule of Law and the Principles of the American Founding:** Contributed to Science Mission Directorate policy SPD-41a (Scientific Information Policy), which governs how publicly funded data are released; ensure portfolio products meet that policy and federal open-data requirements so the public, firefighters, and land managers get free, documented, reliable data (civic-mindedness).
- **ECQ 2 – Driving Efficiency:** Leading the consolidation of existing data production work into a Foundational Data Products budget more than 20\% smaller than its current cost (fiscal responsibility); set designation criteria that retire duplicative products and centralize processing (managing resources, leveraging technology); reused NASA's Senior Review framework for FDP evaluation instead of building a new process; scoping a joint NASA–NOAA Level-0 reprocessing approach to cut duplicate interagency spending.
- **ECQ 3 – Merit and Competence:** Wrote the FDP formulation framework (definition, designation criteria, product specifications, portfolio management), requiring every product to meet NASA Standard Data Product criteria (technical skill, problem solving); serve as Data Systems Lead for active flight missions and airborne campaigns across four centers; selected as the only Headquarters scientist in the inaugural NASA Engineering Development Program cohort (agility and resilience).
- **ECQ 4 – Leading People:** Direct the work of about 10 contractor and center project-office staff, setting priorities, reviewing deliverables, and holding teams to cost and schedule (accountability); selected the FDP Project Manager (executive judgment); direct and mentor an AAAS Science & Technology Policy Fellow, delegating ownership of portfolio workstreams to her; set stretch assignments for the program's operations officer and mentor 1–2 NASA interns each year (developing others).
- **ECQ 5 – Achieving Results:** Moved FDP from concept to a leadership-approved formulation aligned with Earth Science Division priorities and positioned SIPS to transition into it (strategic thinking, operational mindset); identified the AAAS Science & Technology Policy Fellowship as a new way to bring talent into ESDS, now in use (innovation); recognized with the FY26 Headquarters Honor Award for Excellence in National Benefits.
- **TQ 1 – Conservation Financial Assistance, Statutory Compliance, and Risk Management:** Serve as Headquarters award oversight for the ESIP cooperative agreement, reviewing deliverables, spend plans, and compliance with award terms; manage portfolio risk through formal criteria, documented reviews, and corrective direction to project offices; working knowledge of the Wildlife and Sport Fish Restoration (Pittman-Robertson and Dingell-Johnson) programs and NEPA, NHPA, and ESA compliance requirements.
- **TQ 2 – Enterprise Grants, Fiscal, and Portfolio Management:** Direct annual planning, budget allocation, and performance review for a \$40M/yr portfolio spread across four geographically dispersed NASA centers, balancing centralized Headquarters requirements with each project's own mission and user commitments.

**Program Coordinator, Ecological Conservation (AAAS Science & Technology Policy Fellow)**, Earth Science Division\
NASA Headquarters, Washington, DC \textbar{} Aug 2022 – Nov 2024 \textbar{} GS-15 equivalent \textbar{} 40 hrs/wk

- **TQ 1 / TQ 2 – Competitive financial assistance:** Managed the solicitation lifecycle for NASA Ecological Conservation awards: drafted solicitation language (including open-data compliance requirements), ran peer review panels, and supported award selections.
- **ECQ 1 / TQ 2 – Interagency partnerships with DOI, states, and Tribes:** Built the relationships behind a binding Memorandum of Understanding among USGS, NASA, and the National Park Service, and a new center-to-center partnership between USGS Patuxent Wildlife Research Center and NASA Goddard; engaged the Association of Fish and Wildlife Agencies and Western Association of Fish and Wildlife Agencies to align NASA data with state conservation priorities; opened new engagement with Tribal-serving organizations.
- **ECQ 1 – National representation:** Represented NASA on the National Nature Assessment federal steering committee, the National Invasive Species Council, the natural capital accounting interagency working group, and the National Plan for Civil Earth Observations writing team.
- **ECQ 5 – Strategic planning:** Led development of the program's strategic and business plan guiding 1- and 3-year investments; organized national workshops of 75–500 participants.

**Research Ecologist and Mendenhall Postdoctoral Fellow**, U.S. Geological Survey, Lakewood, CO\
Aug 2019 – Aug 2022 \textbar{} GS-0408-12 \textbar{} 40 hrs/wk

- Developed statistical methods and open-source software (bbsAssistant) that put the North American Breeding Bird Survey into wider use by wildlife managers; performance awards in each full fiscal year.

Managed concurrent multi-partner research projects, including applied work for natural resource management on U.S. military installations; trained state natural resource agency staff in data management and geospatial analysis.
